entry.summary: Proposes evaluating the implicit software world model of coding LLMs by predicting execution resources (peak memory, wall-clock time, ranked profiler outputs) beyond control-flow outcomes, using SWE-bench Verified. It finds frontier models perform modestly and brittlely on resource prediction.

entry.title: Retroactive Advantage Correction: Closed-Form V-Trace Bias Correction for Delay-Aware RLHF

author.name: Arnav Raj

entry.summary: Introduces Retroactive Advantage Correction (RAC) for delay-aware RLHF, handling asynchronous slow reward signals (code verifiers, judge ensembles, queued human review) by queuing, aging, and reinjecting clipped residuals into later optimizer steps. Proves the correction is exactly unbiased under full-mass reinjection.

entry.title: Closed-Form Steepest Descent Direction toward Flat Minima: Reducing Upper Bounds on the Loss Hessian Eigenspectrum in Neural Networks

author.name: Yuto Omae, Kazuki Sakai, Yohei Kakimoto, Makoto Sasaki, Yusuke Sakai, Hirotaka Takahashi

entry.summary: Derives the analytic gradient of an existing upper bound (Wolkowicz-Styan) on the loss Hessian's largest eigenvalue, providing a closed-form steepest-descent direction toward flat minima. Connects data and parameter structure to flatness-seeking optimization.

entry.title: ML-Powered LDAP Reconnaissance Detection using Weak Supervision

author.name: Shaefer Drew, Edward Raff, Michael Brautbar, Yaron Zinar, Benjamin Malmberg, Dor Agron, Sagi Sheinfeld, Avraham Kama, Asaf Romano

entry.summary: Develops two ML frameworks using weak supervision to detect malicious LDAP reconnaissance queries against Active Directory, correlating queries with endpoint detections to label large datasets. An industrial case study targeting early-stage threat detection.

entry.title: Anti-Collapse Dynamics and the Emergence of Multi-Time-Scale Learning in Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Lorenzo Livi

entry.summary: This paper introduces the idea that the decay rate of past-input influence in recurrent neural networks is not architecturally fixed but emerges from coupled state and parameter dynamics, settling into either fast-forgetting or slow power-law regimes. Understanding this anti-collapse mechanism could explain when RNNs can learn long-range dependencies efficiently.

entry.title: A Diagnostic Framework and Multi-Evaluator Audit of Evaluator-Driven Preference Dynamics in Self-Adapting LLM Agents

author.name: Liu Zewen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a diagnostic framework (EPC with preference collapse index, coupling matrices, and JS divergence) to detect when proprietary LLM evaluators drift and invalidate measurements, documenting a real GPT-4o May-to-June shift. It warns that evaluator-driven preference dynamics in self-adapting agents can become unstable within weeks.

entry.title: Decision-Value Attribution in Predict-then-Optimize Systems

author.name: Konstantinos Ziliaskopoulos, Alexander Vinel, Alice E. Smith

entry.summary: Decision Value Attribution (DVA) is a Shapley-based framework that attributes the value of a fixed predict-then-optimize pipeline to information sources and parameters, explaining decisions rather than just forecasts. It captures that large forecast changes may not alter decisions while small ones can flip the optimizer's action.

entry.title: Robust Strategic Classification under Decision-Dependent Cost Uncertainty

author.name: Sura Alhanouti, G\"uzin Bayraksan, Parinaz Naghizadeh

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage robust optimization framework for strategic classification where manipulation costs are decision-dependent, meaning today's algorithmic decisions influence tomorrow's gaming costs, relaxing the fixed-cost assumption of prior work. It analyzes robust classifiers under decision-dependent cost uncertainty.

entry.title: KnowsTFM: Knowledge-Informed Fine-Tuning of Small Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Boshko Koloski, Xiangjian Jiang, Senja Pollak, Bla\v{z} \v{S}krlj, Mateja Jamnik, Nikola Simidjievski

entry.summary: KnowsTFM is a knowledge-informed fine-tuning method for small tabular foundation models that incorporates curated relational knowledge from knowledge graphs and banks to improve performance in niche, data-scarce, high-dimensional domains shifted from pretraining. It addresses where tabular foundation models still lose to domain-specific methods.

entry.title: KM-Speaker: Keypoint-Based Style Control for High-Quality Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation and Dialogue Localization

author.name: Arthur Josi, Emeline Got, Abdallah Dib, Luiz Gustavo Hafemann, Rafael M. O. Cruz

entry.summary: Presents KM-Speaker, a keypoint-conditioned flow-based generative framework for speech-driven 3D facial animation that provides both global style guidance and frame-level control for tasks like dialogue localization and dubbing. This achieves high-fidelity motion with production-quality control. It matters for animation and dubbing pipelines.

entry.title: Perspectives on Latent Factor Indeterminacy and its Implications for Data Representation

author.name: Carel F. W. Peeters

entry.summary: Examines latent factor indeterminacy in factor analysis viewed as a minimal generative neural network, arguing that even with known dimension and resolved rotational indeterminacy, the retrieval of causative latent sources remains inherently uncertain. This has implications for interpreting latent representations in generative models. It offers a foundational cautionary perspective on disentanglement.

entry.title: Clinical Reasoning Graphs: Structured Evaluation of LLM Diagnostic Reasoning Reveals Competence Without Consistency

author.name: Nisarg A. Patel (University of California, San Francisco)

entry.summary: Introduces clinical reasoning graphs extracted from LLM diagnostic traces using a domain ontology to evaluate whether models show stable structured reasoning across similar cases. Finds competence without consistency across 750 traces from five models on NEJM cases.

entry.title: CORTEX: High-Quality Cross-Domain Organization of Web-Scale Corpora through Ontological Corpus Graph

author.name: Chengtao Gan, Xiaoke Guo, Yushan Zhu, Zhaoyan Gong, Zhiqiang Liu, Songze Li, Huajun Chen, Wen Zhang

entry.summary: CORTEX organizes web-scale training corpora into a three-layer Ontological Corpus Graph with quality-refined content, a hierarchical ontology, and structured knowledge organization rather than flat document collections. Aims to meet stage-specific data needs for LLM training.

entry.title: GPTNT: Benchmarking Real-Time Collaboration Between Multimodal Agents on Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes

author.name: Amit Parekh, Sabrina McCallum, Kareem Al-Hasan, Malvina Nikandrou, Alessandro Suglia, Ioannis Konstas

entry.summary: Introduces GPTNT, a benchmark built on the cooperative game Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes where two multimodal agents must coordinate under time pressure and information asymmetry to defuse puzzles. Studies collaboration conditions usually examined in isolation.

entry.title: The Complexity Ceiling Benchmark: A Multi-Domain Evaluation of Sequential Reasoning Under Depth Scaling

author.name: Shubh Chapra, Dhruv Kumar, Murari Mandal, Yash Sinha

entry.summary: The Complexity Ceiling Benchmark measures how LLM reasoning decays as required sequential steps grow, fixing task semantics and varying depth across spatial state-tracking, symbolic pointer manipulation, and transitive inference. Finds geometric per-step decay with widely separated domain ceilings, with transitive inference collapsing fastest.

entry.title: UCOB: Learning to Utilize and Evolve Agentic Skills via Credit-Aware On-Policy Bidirectional Self-Distillation

author.name: Songjun Tu, Chengdong Xu, Qichao Zhang, Yiwen Ma, Yaocheng Zhang, Linjing Li, Dong Li, Xiangyuan Lan, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: UCOB learns to utilize and evolve agentic skills via credit-aware on-policy bidirectional self-distillation, treating skill-conditioned and no-skill prompts as two views of the same model and using the higher-return view as a local teacher. Addresses the fragility of the privileged-teacher assumption when retrieved skills sometimes mislead.

entry.title: Consistency as Inductive Bias: Learning Cross-View Invariance for Robust Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Xin Zou, Haolin Deng, Yibo Yan, Shuliang Liu, Kening Zheng, Zhiwei Jin, Chen Chen, Haonan Lu, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: ConsistRoll adds cross-view consistency as an inductive bias to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for multimodal LLMs, reusing GRPO group sampling so that semantically invariant views of the same instance produce the same answer. It targets a gap where standard RLVR rewards each view independently, providing little learning signal once within-view rewards saturate.

entry.title: LWDrive: Layer-Wise World-Model-Guided Vision-Language Model Planning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chen Yang, Yuhao Wei, Ze Xu, Ziheng Zou, Shuang Liang, Delin Ouyang, Lingfeng Qi, Jie Li, Guofa Li

entry.summary: LWDrive uses layer-wise world-model guidance to refine coarse VLM-generated trajectories for end-to-end autonomous driving, treating the VLM output as an intent-aware coarse plan and progressively refining candidates with geometric and future-aware constraints. It aims to overcome the geometric imprecision of direct VLM trajectory generation.

entry.title: Variance Reduction on the Camera Axis: Multi-View Score Distillation for 3D

author.name: Marian Lupascu, Mihai Sorin Stupariu, Ionut Mironica

entry.summary: MV-SDI reduces the variance of score distillation gradients in 2D-to-3D generation by aggregating K view samples per optimization step at a fixed UNet budget, isolating the sampling axis without retraining the diffusion prior. This improves global shape consistency while keeping the prior unchanged.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Iteration Distillation for Robust IHD Screening: The IDNet Framework and A New Benchmark

author.name: Yongchang Gao, Junjie Pang, Shuaiyu Yang, Yusheng Yang, Xichao Jia, Shaojie Li, Hongfei Zhang, Jia Mu

entry.summary: IDNet is a multimodal framework for ischemic heart disease screening from color fundus photography, using a Cross-Modal Distillation Aggregator with learnable queries to integrate left-eye, right-eye, and sparse clinical features and mitigate the imbalance between visual and tabular dimensions. It also contributes a reproducible 50,410-image UK Biobank benchmark.

entry.title: Latent Noise Mask for Reducing Visual Redundancy in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kai Jiang, Ruishu Zhu, Siqi Huang, Hongyuan Zhang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Lens (Latent Noise Mask) is a question-conditioned visual evidence purification framework for multimodal LLMs that uses a lightweight Lens Evidence Token to score which visual tokens support the current question and preserve them during decoding, injecting noise to suppress redundant tokens. It addresses dilution of question-relevant cues by dense redundant image tokens that hurts fine-grained reasoning.

entry.title: Lifted Causal Inference

author.name: Malte Luttermann, Tanya Braun, Ralf M\"oller, Marcel Gehrke

entry.summary: Introduces parametric causal factor graphs and a Lifted Causal Inference algorithm to compute causal effects efficiently in relational domains by exploiting indistinguishabilities. It provides formal semantics for interventions and substantial speedups over propositional inference.

entry.title: DataStates-LLM: Scalable Checkpointing for Transformer Models Using Composable State Providers

author.name: Avinash Maurya, M. Mustafa Rafique, Franck Cappello, Bogdan Nicolae

entry.summary: Presents DataStates-LLM, a scalable checkpointing system for trillion-parameter transformer training that uses composable state providers to handle the 3D heterogeneity of distributed model state rather than opaque binary blobs. It improves resilience, suspend-resume, and training-trajectory inspection.

entry.title: PEBS: Per-rater Empirical-Bayes Shrinkage for RLHF Reward-Model Calibration

author.name: Arnav Raj

entry.summary: Proposes PEBS, a per-rater empirical-Bayes shrinkage estimator that fits per-annotator affine calibrators and shrinks toward the population mean to fix RLHF reward-model calibration, which otherwise collapses diverse raters into one average fit. Reduces within-user held-out RMSE by 8.58% in closed form without retraining.

entry.title: From Signals to Transfer: A Factorised Study of Probe-Based Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models

author.name: Ponhvoan Srey, Xiaobao Wu, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Quang Minh Nguyen, Duc Anh Vu, Anh Tuan Luu

entry.summary: Conducts a factorised study of probe-based uncertainty estimation for hallucination detection in LLMs under matched conditions, disentangling feature design, training data, and evaluation. Finds raw hidden states are hard to beat in-domain but structured compressed features are more robust under distribution shift.

entry.title: Room for Error: Large-Scale Simulation of Over-the-Air Acoustic Attacks

author.name: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil Marchant, Jiani Xie, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: Introduces a high-throughput reality simulation framework for over-the-air acoustic adversarial attacks against voice control systems, running over 8 million adversarial evaluations to incorporate room geometry and acoustic factors usually abstracted away. Demonstrates that acoustic awareness substantially changes attack effectiveness.

entry.title: End-to-End Dynamic Sparsity for Resource-Adaptive LLM Inference

author.name: Yuhang Chen, Jinhao Duan, Ruichen Zhang, Mingfu Liang, Xiaohan Wei, Yunchen Pu, Fei Tian, Chonglin Sun, Parish Aggarwal, Frank Shyu, Luke Simon, Sandeep Pandey, Tianlong Chen, Xi Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Learning to Allocate (L2A), an end-to-end framework for resource-adaptive LLM inference that formulates inference as a constrained allocation problem rather than conditioning only on input difficulty, handling dynamic cloud conditions like spot preemption and tiered QoS. Enables dynamic sparsity to avoid crashes or wasted compute.

entry.title: SHIFT: Gate-Modulated Activation Steering for Knowledge Conflict Mitigation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Ruochang Li, Pengcheng Huang, Zhenghao Liu, Yukun Yan, Huiyuan Xie, Yu Gu, Ge Yu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Introduces SHIFT, a gate-modulated activation steering framework to mitigate knowledge conflicts between retrieved context and parametric knowledge in RAG, avoiding the cascading side effects of neuron-level editing approaches. It reformulates neuron editing as a steering problem to preserve general capabilities.

entry.title: Towards Improved Anomaly Detection for Cloud Cybersecurity via Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Manu Nandan, TJ Jaymes, Michael Brautbar, Edward Raff

entry.summary: Presents an industrial self-supervised graph-neural-network approach on AWS CloudTrail logs to surface suspicious cloud events with adaptive anomaly scoring. Aims to reduce false positives compared to static heuristics without periodic retraining.

entry.title: RGLD: Randomized Global-Local Density Estimation for Tabular Anomaly Detection

author.name: Quanling Zhao, Jiaying Yang, Ye Tian, Josh Victoria, Zhijun Wang, Pietro Mercati, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: Introduces RGLD, a randomized global-local density estimator for unsupervised tabular anomaly detection combining a global random-feature density branch with a local neighbor branch. Aims for accuracy, robustness across heterogeneous datasets, and computational efficiency.

entry.title: What Drives the Inlier-Memorization Effect? A Theory of Outlier Detection via Early Training Dynamics

author.name: Kunwoong Kim, Dongha Kim

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical explanation for the inlier-memorization effect—why deep models memorize normal inliers before outliers during early training—using a simple autoencoder analysis under mild assumptions. It strengthens the theoretical foundation for unsupervised outlier detection.

entry.title: Bandwidth Selection in Kernel Density Estimation for Model Calibration

author.name: Han Zhou, Teodora Popordanoska, Matthew Blaschko

entry.summary: This paper introduces Risk Alignment, a framework for selecting kernel bandwidth in KDE-based model calibration by aligning KDE-reconstructed risk with empirical risk, since standard MLE bandwidth selection fails for calibration. It provides theoretical justification for improved calibration estimation.

entry.title: Discovering Collaboration from Novelty: Random Network Distillation for Clustered Federated Learning

author.name: Davide Domini, Gianluca Aguzzi, Ivana Dusparic, Danilo Pianini, Mirko Viroli

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight clustered federated learning method using Random Network Distillation prediction error as a novelty signal to discover client similarity before training, decoupling clustering from the main loop. This reduces compute and communication for non-IID federated settings. It offers an efficient route to client grouping.

entry.title: Reproducing FACTER: Fairness via Conformal Thresholding and Prompt Repair

author.name: Oscar Mir\'o L\'opez-Feliu, Daimy van Loo, Xanthos Kekkos, Mikel Blom, Clara Rus

entry.summary: A reproducibility study of FACTER, a framework enforcing fairness and coverage in LLM recommendations via conformal thresholding and prompt repair, finding divergence in recommendation utility traced to underspecified target-set evaluation and proposing a constrained re-ranking evaluation. This strengthens evaluation rigor. It matters for reliable fairness claims.

entry.title: FedLAS: Feature-Modulated Bidirectional Label Smoothing for Neural Network Calibration

author.name: Thiru Thillai Nadarasar Bahavan, Sachith Seneviratne, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: Introduces FedLAS, a feature-modulated bidirectional label smoothing method for neural network calibration that adapts smoothing per-sample to address both overconfidence and under-confidence, relaxing the uniform assumptions of standard and margin-based label smoothing. This improves calibration across diverse sample difficulties. It matters for trustworthy classifier confidence.

entry.title: Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering

author.name: Chengfeng Zhao, Yuqiao Tan, Shizhu He, Yequan Wang, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: Neural Procedural Memory (NPM) is a training-free framework giving LLM agents persistent procedural memory through implicit activation steering rather than textual RAG instructions, addressing the text-action disconnect. Aims to activate internal representations needed for correct task execution.

entry.title: IHDec: Divergence-Steered Contrastive Decoding for Securing Multi-Turn Instruction Hierarchies

author.name: Nicole Geumheon Liu, Haeun Jang, Yonghyun Jun, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: IHDec is a training-free contrastive decoding method that uses Jensen-Shannon divergence to detect and correct instruction-hierarchy violations in multi-turn settings, addressing role-influence inversion. Secures priority ordering without expensive fine-tuning.

entry.title: PolicyGuard: A Dialogue-Grounded Sub-Agent Verifier for Policy Adherence in LLM Agents

author.name: Seongjae Kang, Taehyung Yu, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: PolicyGuard is a dialogue-grounded sub-agent verifier ensuring LLM agents adhere to organizational policies across multi-turn workflows, using full conversation context, self-reasoning, and conversation-specific remediation. Reframes policy adherence beyond simple action-blocking safeguards.

entry.title: RainODE: Continuous-Time Precipitation Forecasting with Latent Neural ODEs

author.name: Yeeun Seong, Doyi Kim, Minseok Seo, Changick Kim

entry.summary: RainODE reformulates precipitation nowcasting as a continuous-time dynamical system, modeling rainfall evolution in latent space with a Neural ODE to enable derivative-consistent temporal dynamics at arbitrary resolution. It augments the deterministic ODE to capture non-advective intensity changes like localized growth and decay.

entry.title: StrucTab: A Structured Optimization Framework for Table Parsing

author.name: Gengluo Li, Shangpin Peng, Chengquan Zhang, Binghong Wu, Hao Feng, Weinong Wang, Pengyuan Lyu, Huawen Shen, Xingyu Wan, Zhuotao Tian, Han Hu, Can Ma, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: StrucTab is a table parsing model that converts table images into structured representations using intermediate structural supervision and reward decomposition, rather than supervising only the final output. It addresses unstable RL reward designs for VLM-based table parsing.

entry.title: Shell-Supervised Gaussian Splatting for Urban Real-to-Sim Reconstruction

author.name: Yuan Yang, Peijun Lu, Fangzhou Lu, Sai Fan, Siqi Yan, Chenyuan Zhang, Haobo Liang, Yichen Wang

entry.summary: Shell-Supervised Gaussian Splatting reconstructs urban facades for embodied AI real-to-sim use by aligning an external structural shell to provide lightweight geometric supervision for video-driven Gaussian reconstruction. It targets unstable surface geometry from glass, reflections, and repetitive low-texture facades that produce plausible renderings but poor collision geometry.

entry.title: T2LDM++: A Self-Conditioned Representation Guided Diffusion Model for Realistic Text-to-LiDAR Scene Generation

author.name: Wentao Qu, Qi Zhang, Chenxu Wang, Guofeng Mei, Yongfei Liu, Xiaoshui Huang, Gim Hee Lee, Liang Xiao

entry.summary: T2LDM++ is a text-to-LiDAR diffusion model with self-conditioned representation guidance that alleviates object over-smoothing via a guidance network providing reconstruction-based soft supervision to the denoising network. It addresses the scarcity of text-LiDAR pairs that causes over-smoothed scenes and limited controllability.

entry.title: DrivenMorph: Bridging Attention Mechanism and Variational Image Registration via Difference Modeling

author.name: Mingke Li, Jianping Zhang, Jinqiu Deng

entry.summary: DrivenMorph bridges attention mechanisms with variational image registration by incorporating difference modeling as a physically inspired inductive bias, computing a driving force from latent feature differences and using a neural Demons layer to simulate force-displacement interactions. It aims for physically explainable, fine-grained deformation control in medical image registration.

entry.title: Import AI 463: Self-improving robots; a 10k Chinese GPU cluster; and an elegiac essay for the human era

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: An issue of Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter covering NVIDIA's ENPIRE framework, a harness that gives physical robots an autonomous experiment-and-improvement loop analogous to AI agents, plus items on a large Chinese GPU cluster and a reflective essay on the human era. It surfaces and contextualizes notable developments in robotics self-improvement and compute. A credible aggregation with light original commentary.

entry.title: Understanding Rollout Error in Graph World Models

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: Studies long-horizon rollout error in Graph World Models, formulating a unified fixed-edge and dynamic-edge framework and deriving graph-valued rollout bounds that separate topology-induced from model-induced error amplification. Introduces a joint node-edge operator.

entry.title: Class-frequency Guided Noise Schedule for Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiequan Cui, Beier Zhu, Qingshan Xu, Xiaojuan Qi, Bei Yu, Hanwang Zhang

entry.summary: Examines correlations between class frequency and multi-scale noise schedules in diffusion models, showing low-frequency classes face larger low-density regions and worse score estimation while high-frequency classes dominate the score space. Proposes a class-frequency guided noise schedule to improve generation of rare classes.

entry.title: Enhancing Numerical Prediction in LLMs via Smooth MMD Alignment

author.name: Zhuo Zuo, Li Yue, Wenhao Zheng, Chenpeng Wang, Xianggen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Smooth Maximum Mean Discrepancy (SMMD) to improve numerical prediction in LLMs by incorporating value-distance kernels over numeric tokens and graph-based smoothness, replacing standard cross-entropy that ignores the metric structure of numbers. Aligns predicted numeric distributions to targets via kernel matching.

entry.title: RS-Diffuser: Risk-Sensitive Diffusion Planning with Distributional Value Guidance

author.name: Shiqiang Gong

entry.summary: Proposes RS-Diffuser, a risk-sensitive offline diffusion planning framework combining diffusion-based trajectory generation with distributional value critics to account for rare catastrophic outcomes that risk-neutral planners overlook. Targets safety-critical applications where online exploration is costly.

entry.title: On design-unbiased algorithmic Machine Learning

author.name: Li-Chun Zhang, Siu-Ming Tam, Luis Sanguiao-Sande, Wesley Yung, Anders Holmberg

entry.summary: Studies conditions under which standard ML algorithms (kNN, random forest) can yield design-unbiased prediction for finite populations, relevant to official statistics. Examines sampling, tuning, and out-of-sample performance assessment.

entry.title: On Surrogate Modeling of Static Response of AM Short-Fiber Thermoplastics Using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Pharindra Pathak (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Vipin Kumar (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Trenton M. Ricks (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Suhasini Gururaja (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Siddhartha Srivastava (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University)

entry.summary: Develops a graph-neural-network surrogate for predicting the static mechanical response of additively manufactured short-fiber thermoplastic composites, capturing mesoscale interactions of fiber orientation, clustering, and porosity. Aims to replace computationally intractable finite-element models.

entry.title: Structured Proper Loss Geometries for Multiclass Classification: Theory and Controlled Empirical Evaluation

author.name: Soumyadip Sarkar

entry.summary: Studies three multiclass proper-scoring objectives with different loss geometries (CAPM quadratic Bregman, HPG strongly convex log-cosh, APMS with annealed margin penalty), deriving regret, curvature, and gradient bounds. Provides controlled multi-seed empirical evaluation on standard and synthetic datasets.

entry.title: A Mathematical Optimization Approach for Expert-Informed Bayesian Best Subset Selection

author.name: Nolan Alexander, Henning Mortveit

entry.summary: Presents EBBS, a mixed-integer optimization method for best-subset feature selection that incorporates domain-expert probability estimates of feature relevance directly into the objective. Bridges classical sparse selection with Bayesian expert priors.

entry.title: ScaleAware-JEPA: Latent Representation for Discovery in Multiscale Physical Fields

author.name: Guang-Xing Li

entry.summary: ScaleAware-JEPA constructs dense label-free latent coordinates for continuous physical fields by using Constrained Diffusion Decomposition to define scale-aware masking geometry for a JEPA objective. It targets discovery in multiscale scientific fields where useful coordinates are unknown in advance.

entry.title: RoAd-RL: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Adithya Mohan, Daniel Kriegl, Torsten Sch\"on

entry.summary: RoAd-RL is an open-source benchmarking framework providing unified abstractions for policies, attacks, defenses, and robustness metrics in adversarial reinforcement learning, with reproducible pipelines integrated with Stable-Baselines3 and Gymnasium. It evaluates DQN, PPO, and SAC under 192 attack-defense configurations.

entry.title: Heads, Not Backbones: Output Heads Dominate Architectures on Fat-Tailed Returns

author.name: Sichao He, Yansong Zhang

entry.summary: This study compares four forecasting backbones under three output heads (point, single-Gaussian, mixture-density) on fat-tailed S&P 500 returns, finding that the output head choice dominates the backbone architecture for probabilistic accuracy. It argues practitioners should focus on heads rather than backbones for heavy-tailed financial forecasting.

entry.title: Curvature-Guided Sheaf Diffusion for Unsupervised Community Detection on Heterophilic Graphs

author.name: Feifan Wang

entry.summary: Curvature-Guided Sheaf Diffusion is a fully unsupervised community-detection algorithm for heterophilic graphs that uses discrete Forman-Ricci edge curvature as a single topological signal propagated through a sheaf-diffusion encoder trained with label-free structural losses. It targets the hard problem where connected nodes belong to different classes.

entry.title: Event-Conditioned Diagnostics of Kinematic, Contact, and Object-Permanence Fields in Passive Object-State World Models

author.name: Yang Liu, Yuming Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled diagnostic protocol to study how passive object-state world models encode event-regime information (kinematics, contact, object permanence) in their latent dynamics, testing whether field-aligned components have functional prediction consequences. This probes the internal organization of physical world models. It matters for interpretable world modeling.

entry.title: Memory-Managed Long-Context Attention: A Preliminary Study of Editable Request-Local Memory

author.name: Junyi Zou, Avrova Donz

entry.summary: A preliminary study of memory-managed long-context attention that separates a fast recurrent or sparse backbone from explicit editable request-local memory slots with query-time sparse fallback, showing pure fixed-state or sparse methods fail at overwrite/distractor tasks. This argues for explicit editable memory in long-context models. It matters for reliable long-term memory.

entry.title: KbSD: Knowledge Boundary aware Self-Distillation for Behavioral Calibration in Agentic Search

author.name: Tao Feng, Xinke Jiang, Chao Wu

entry.summary: KbSD uses knowledge-boundary-aware self-distillation with dense token-level supervision, sparse outcome rewards, and quadrant-adaptive optimization to calibrate when agentic search should trust memory, retrieve, or abstain. Tackles reward sparsity in knowledge boundary calibration.

entry.title: Are We Measuring Strategy or Phrasing? The Gap Between Surface- and Approach-Level Diversity in LLM Math Reasoning

author.name: Sangmook Lee, Minbeom Kim, Jeonghye Kim, Dohyung Kim, Sojeong Rhee, Kyomin Jung

entry.summary: Distinguishes surface-level (phrasing) from approach-level (strategy) diversity in LLM math reasoning, showing common diversity metrics are poor proxies for strategic diversity. Finds approach-diverse candidate sets improve test-time scaling.

entry.title: The Interference Gap: Comparing Retrieval Bounds in Human Memory and RAG Systems

author.name: Dongxin Guo, Jikun Wu, Siu-Ming Yiu

entry.summary: Applies a unified signal detection theory framework to compare retrieval bounds in human episodic memory and RAG systems under semantic interference, finding humans have lower interference sensitivity than dense retrieval. Cognitively-inspired HippoRAG falls between the two.

entry.title: LUMEN: Cost-Transparent Multi-Agent Pipeline for Automated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

author.name: Yen-Hsun Huang (Department of Education, Taipei Veterans General Hospital, Taipei, Taiwan), Yu-Shiou Lin (Department of Psychiatry, Taipei Veterans General Hospital, Taipei, Taiwan)

entry.summary: LUMEN is an open-source 11-agent pipeline automating six phases of systematic reviews and meta-analyses with model routing, and is the first to report end-to-end cost transparency across phases. Examines cost-quality trade-offs in automated evidence synthesis.

entry.title: Detecting Clinical Hallucinations in LVLMs via Counterfactual Visual Grounding Uncertainty

author.name: Xiao Song, Haonan Qin, Zhaoxu Zhang, Jiong Zhang, Yuqi Fang, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: Presents a vision-traceable hallucination detection framework for clinical LVLMs that grounds verifiable entities on images using a medical grounding verifier with counterfactual perturbation for uncertainty estimation. Requires no model modification or internal access.

entry.title: Animation2Code: Evaluating Temporal Visual Reasoning in Video-to-Code Generation

author.name: Anya Ji, Abhijith Varma Mudunuri, David M. Chan, Alane Suhr

entry.summary: Animation2Code is a benchmark of 1,069 web animation videos paired with HTML/CSS/JS implementations to evaluate temporal visual reasoning in video-to-code generation. Proposes appearance and temporal similarity metrics to disentangle visual fidelity from temporal alignment.

entry.title: Mixture of Debaters: Learn to Debate at Architectural Level in Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Dayong Liang, Kaisong Gong, Yi Cai, Changmeng Zheng, Xiao-Yong Wei

entry.summary: Mixture of Debaters (MoD) enables dynamic self-debate within a single model using the Mixture-of-Experts paradigm, with dual-routing decoupling role allocation from process flow and momentum switching to reduce expert-switch jitter. Avoids multiple model copies needed by prior debate frameworks.

entry.title: Know Before You Fetch: Calibrated Retrieval-Budget Allocation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zhe Dong (University of Maine at Presque Isle), Fang Qin (Stanford University), Manish Shah (Independent Researcher), Yicheng Wang (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: This work reframes adaptive RAG as calibrated retrieval-budget allocation, deciding per query whether to answer closed-book, retrieve a compact or full context, or abstain, based on calibrated probabilities of correctness. The contribution is a probability interface over existing uncertainty signals enabling graded context selection and latency tradeoffs.

entry.title: SUMO: Segment and Track Any Motion with Nonlinear State Space Models

author.name: Kexin Tian, Sixu Li, Keshu Wu, Yang Zhou, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: SUMO is a zero-shot, training-free framework that unifies visual object tracking and moving object segmentation by integrating a robotics-inspired nonlinear state space model with vision-based segmentation. A Selective Unscented Filter handles complex nonlinear object dynamics for more accurate state estimation.

entry.title: Rigel: Self-Distilled Score Adaptation for Image and Video Captioning Evaluation

author.name: Shuitsu Koyama, Kazuki Matsuda, Yuiga Wada, Shinnosuke Hirano, Daichi Yashima, Komei Sugiura

entry.summary: Rigel is an automatic evaluation metric for image and video captioning based on self-distilled score adaptation, employing an evaluation-specific scoring head distilled from a frozen LLM to better align with human judgments. It addresses the mismatch between large-vocabulary language modeling and scoring over a small label set in LLM-as-a-Judge metrics.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Energy Aggregation for Mobile 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Xiaobiao Du, YuAn Wang, Hao Li, Bosheng Wang, Xun Sun, Xin Yu

entry.summary: Flux-GS is a real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting method for mobile platforms that reduces inference and storage overhead from high-order spherical harmonics via a Monte Carlo Specular Energy Aggregator, sampling third-order radiance residuals into a compact latent space. It preserves salient lighting without expensive distillation or pre-training.

entry.title: CylindTrack: Depth-Aware Cylindrical Motion Modeling for Panoramic Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Buyin Deng, Kai Luo, Lingxin Huang, Xinqi Liu, Fei Cheng, Hang Zheng, Liming Yin, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: CylindTrack addresses panoramic multi-object tracking by introducing depth-aware cylindrical motion modeling, handling the periodic horizontal domain of equirectangular video that breaks planar motion assumptions and makes IoU association unreliable near the 0/360-degree seam. It targets large field-of-view embodied perception with frequent interactions and scale variation.

entry.title: A Dual-domain Refinement Network with FBP-based Jacobian Learning for Sparse-view Dual-Energy CT Material Decomposition

author.name: Qian Liu, Xiaohong Fan, Ke Chen, Chong Chen, Shuaikang Wang, Jianping Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a dual-domain refinement network with FBP-based Jacobian learning for sparse-view dual-energy CT material decomposition, explicitly incorporating the Jacobian operator from the nonlinear forward model and replacing convolution-based sparsity priors with global structural modeling. It tackles the nonlinear, ill-posed decomposition problem under reduced radiation exposure.

entry.title: Intermediate Text Representation Guided Text-to-Image Generation for Enhancing One-and-Only Alignment

author.name: Soyoun Won, Aryan Yazdan Parast, Basim Azam, Jean Honorio, Naveed Akhtar

entry.summary: SkelEM is a self-supervised axial super-resolution framework for anisotropic volume microscopy that decouples training signals, optimizing a frozen topological skeleton network and a diffusion refiner with disjoint objectives to separate low-frequency topology from high-frequency detail. It addresses the trilemma of smoothed regression, hallucination, and slow inference.

entry.title: Cross-Resolution Semantic Transfer for Robust Text-to-Image Retrieval in Low-Resolution Surveillance

author.name: Wenjie Qian, Bin Yang, Xiao Wang, Wenke Huang, Ling Mei, Xin Xu, Mang Ye

entry.summary: Cross-Resolution Semantic Transfer (CRST) is a CLIP-style framework for robust text-to-image person re-identification under low-resolution surveillance, addressing Evidence Reliability Collapse where degraded tokens fail text grounding and Ranking Distribution Drift from mixed-resolution galleries. It uses resolution-conditioned reasoning, text-guided refinement, and a cross-resolution alignment module.

entry.title: When Does Personality Composition Matter for Multi-Agent LLM Teams?

author.name: Aryan Keluskar, Amrita Bhattacharjee, Huan Liu

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether personality prompting (e.g., agreeableness traits) of LLM agents affects objective task outcomes across coding, research collaboration, and bargaining domains. It finds that personality effects on performance are context-dependent rather than universal.

entry.title: Grounded Iterative Language Planning: How Parameterized World Models Reduce Hallucination Propagation in LLM Agents

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: Compares agent-based versus parameterized world models for LLM agents, introducing operational hallucination metrics and proposing Grounded Iterative Language Planning (GILP) that trains a small parameterized backbone to reduce hallucination propagation. Evaluated on graph-structured planning benchmarks.

entry.title: GRAFT: Biological Graph and Hypergraph Benchmarks for Linked Gene Expression and Phenotypic Trait Prediction in Arabidopsis thaliana

author.name: Manuel Serna-Aguilera, Vanshika Jindal, Fiona L. Goggin, Jiamei Li, Aranyak Goswami, Alexander Bucksch, Suxing Liu, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: Presents GRAFT, biological graph and hypergraph benchmarks linking gene expression to phenotypic traits in Arabidopsis thaliana for the genome-to-phenome prediction challenge. It addresses the lack of datasets that jointly link gene expression and trait data.

entry.title: The Context-Ready Transformer

author.name: Mahesh Godavarti

entry.summary: Introduces the context-ready transformer, a recurrent architecture that pre-contextualizes each token via a correction network combining cached past context with the current embedding before it enters a transformer block. It unrolls training in parallel and allows converting pretrained transformers into this recurrent form.

entry.title: Flexformer: Flexible Linear Transformer with Learnable Attention Kernel

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Feng Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Flexformer, a flexible linear transformer that learns attention kernels in a fully data-driven manner by treating random Fourier feature spectral frequencies as trainable parameters. Develops stationary and nonstationary variants, with the latter offering greater expressiveness while maintaining linear complexity.

entry.title: NLL-Guided Full-Attention Layer Selection for Training-Free Sliding-Window Adaptation

author.name: Qiong Tang, Xiangkun Hu, Xiangyang Liu, Yiran Chen, Yunfan Shao

entry.summary: Proposes NLL-guided layer selection, a training-free method that decides which layers should retain full attention in hybrid attention models by measuring negative log-likelihood degradation on answer tokens when each layer switches to sliding-window attention. Achieves 64.6% accuracy on LongMemEval with only a quarter of full-attention layers.

entry.title: Entropy Regularized Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Stochastic Differential Games in a Regime-Switching Jump-Diffusion Process

author.name: Congde Hu, Zhuo Jin, Danping Li, Lin Xu

entry.summary: Proposes an entropy-regularized RL framework for zero-sum stochastic differential games in regime-switching jump-diffusion processes, deriving coupled HJBI equations for equilibrium strategies. Targets robustness to parameter misspecification and structural shifts in continuous-time settings.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Orchestrating Collaborative Knowledge Tracing with Hierarchical Semantic Alignment

author.name: Xinjin Li, Mengyue Wang, Yuzhen Lin, Pengbin Feng, Ziqi Sha, Yeyang Zhou, Yu Ma

entry.summary: Proposes MOSAIC for knowledge tracing, using a frozen LLM to generate context-aware embeddings and hierarchical prediction prompts capturing collaborative signals and peer interactions, combined with sequential modeling. Addresses shallow ID-based representations and single-granularity mastery estimation.

entry.title: Nonlinear mixture model motivated subspace clustering

author.name: Ivica Kopriva

entry.summary: Derives the linear union-of-subspaces model for subspace clustering from a nonlinear mixture model via Taylor expansion, establishing correspondences between smoothness order, subspace dimension, anchor counts, and representation sparsity. Enables estimation of bounds on subspace dimension.

entry.title: Not All Objectives Are Born Equal: Priority-Constrained Descent for Hierarchical Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Dara Varam, Mohamed I. Alhajri

entry.summary: Priority-Constrained Descent (PCD) is a gradient-based optimization framework that respects an explicit hierarchy among objectives, preserving primary descent direction while allowing minimal distortion for secondary goals via a single parameter. It addresses the symmetry problem in multi-objective optimization where objectives are treated as equally important.

entry.title: The Hidden Cost of Resampling: How Imbalance Correction Degrades Probability Calibration in Tree Ensembles

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: This work shows that imbalance-correction resampling like SMOTE and undersampling degrades probability calibration in tree ensembles by distorting the training prior, quantifying the effect across five datasets and providing fixes. It offers practical guidance on when calibration damage matters for class-imbalanced classification.

entry.title: T3R: Deeper Test-Time Adaptation for Graph Neural Networks via Gradient Rotation

author.name: Huy Truong, Alexander Lazovik, Victoria Degeler

entry.summary: T3R is a test-time training method for graph neural networks that uses multiple Rotograd matrices to improve task affinity between target and auxiliary tasks and a gradient rotation technique for deeper parameter adaptation under distribution shift. It overcomes the shallow-update limitation of conventional test-time training.

entry.title: DreamForge-World 0.1 Preview: A Low-Compute Real-Time Controllable World Model

author.name: Daniyel Ayupov, Artur Markov-Tsoy

entry.summary: DreamForge-World 0.1 Preview is a low-compute real-time controllable world model adapting an autoregressive video stack with a residual action pathway, supporting live keyboard/mouse control, multimodal initialization, and minute-scale interactive rollouts at 480p reaching 14-15 FPS on a single RTX 4090. It focuses on consumer-GPU runtime rather than frontier-scale simulation.

entry.title: ITSPACE: Monotone Gaussian Optimal Transport Updates

author.name: Woojoo Na, Jennifer Dy

entry.summary: Introduces ITSPACE, a proximal majorization-minimization method for optimizing the exact Bures-Wasserstein optimal-transport objective on covariance matrices via closed-form square-root updates with monotone decrease guarantees. It targets domain adaptation and Gaussian embeddings. This offers principled, stable covariance alignment.

entry.title: Zero-Label Driving Scenario Complexity Detection via Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture

author.name: Santosh Jaiswal

entry.summary: Trains a minimal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture on agent-state driving data and uses temporal prediction error as a zero-shot, label-free complexity score that identifies safety-critical driving scenarios. This avoids costly annotation or rule engineering. It matters for autonomous-driving scenario mining.

entry.title: A Zero-Shot Deep Image Prior Framework for Denoising and Deconvolution in Fluorescence Microscopy

author.name: Xiangyu Qian, Jing Liu, Yunqing Tang, Luru Dai, Qiushi Li

entry.summary: Proposes SDIP, a zero-shot deep image prior framework that sequentially denoises and deconvolves fluorescence microscopy images without external training data, using sequential autoencoding regularization and a wavelet-based RLG-DIP module. This avoids paired-data requirements. It matters for quantitative microscopy restoration.

entry.title: LoRA-Tuned Large Language Models for Dementia Detection via Multi-View Speech-Derived Features

author.name: Jonghyeon Park, Olivier Jiyoun Jung, Myungwoo Oh

entry.summary: Proposes a LoRA-tuned LLM performing structured multi-view reasoning over four speech-derived signals (ASR transcripts with pauses, discourse cues, fluency statistics, phonology) for dementia detection from spontaneous speech. This integrates heterogeneous cognitive symptom evidence. It matters for non-invasive cognitive screening.

entry.title: Adaptive Iterative Hard Thresholding for Online High-dimensional Quantile Regression

author.name: Zitian Zhou, Nan Lin

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Iterative Hard Thresholding (AIHT) for online high-dimensional sparse regression, separating support discovery from local refinement by delaying then increasing thresholding frequency, with theory for online quantile regression. This preserves sparsity under sequential updates. It matters for streaming high-dimensional estimation.

entry.title: A Task-Driven and Quality-Assured Agent Framework for SAR Data Generation

author.name: Xuanting Wu, Fan Zhanga, Fei Ma, Ling Guan, Guochun Ma, Yongsheng Zhou

entry.summary: Presents SAGA, a schema-grounded, benefit-aware agent framework for task-oriented SAR data generation and augmentation that extracts dataset facts, validates schemas, selects augmentation strategies, and validates generated samples from natural-language requests and heterogeneous inputs. This automates fragmented SAR augmentation workflows. It matters for robust SAR interpretation models.

entry.title: A3M: Adaptive, Adversarial and Multi-Objective Learning for Strategic Bidding in Repeated Auctions

author.name: Junhan Li, Yuxin Zhang, Haoran Wang, Minghao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes A3M, an adaptive deep RL framework for strategic bidding in repeated multi-unit auctions with bandit feedback, combining an actor-critic backbone, opponent modeling via fictitious play against non-stationary adversaries, and multi-objective reward design. This overcomes rigid explore-then-exploit and stationarity assumptions. It matters for robust online auction strategy.

entry.title: Resolution Thresholds in VLM Detection of Harmful ASCII Art Across Construction Modes and Languages

author.name: Yikai Hua, Peter West

entry.summary: Investigates how image resolution affects vision-language models' ability to detect harmful content disguised as ASCII art across eight construction modes and two languages. Identifies systematic detection-failure thresholds, exposing a content-moderation vulnerability.

entry.title: Parametric Skills

author.name: Xuan Zhao, Haonan He, Qingyu Yang, Minglei Li, Jingqi Ye, Zelin Tan, Bo Wan, Peng Ye

entry.summary: ParametricSkills converts free-form textual skills into model parameters at test time, enabling context-free skill exploitation that avoids difficulties locating and following instructions in long contexts. Targets improved agentic skill utilization.

entry.title: Regime-Aware Peer Specialization for Robust RAG under Heterogeneous Knowledge Conflicts

author.name: Bo Wang, Heyan Huang, Yaolin Li, Yanghao Zhou, Jiahao Teng, Ziyi Yang, Ge Shi, Chong Feng

entry.summary: RAPS-DA proposes regime-aware peer specialization for RAG, splitting knowledge conflicts into grounding, arbitration, and adversarial regimes to avoid conflating incompatible learning signals. Improves robustness across a reliability spectrum of retrieved context.

entry.title: LLM-Ideoplasticity: Measuring Ideological Plasticity in the Political Behavior of LLMs as a Context-Conditioned Distribution

author.name: Adib Sakhawat, Syed Rifat Raiyan, Tahsin Islam, Takia Farhin, Hasan Mahmud, Md Kamrul Hasan

entry.summary: Argues an LLM's political ideology is a context-conditioned distribution rather than a fixed point, evaluating nine models across six contextual axes using validated political-science projection models. Finds high sensitivity to persuasive framing and language while a cohort-level central tendency persists.

entry.title: Mandol: An Agglomerative Agent Memory System for Long-Term Conversations

author.name: Yuhan Zhang (Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Zhiyuan Guo (Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Ziheng Zeng (Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Wei Wang (Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Wentao Wu (Microsoft Research), Lijie Xu (Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: Mandol is a unified, memory-native architecture for long-term conversational agents that consolidates fragmented vector and graph memory into a single hierarchical model to reduce cross-database latency and retrieval noise. It adds token-budget control to improve both accuracy and efficiency over RAG-style memory.

entry.title: SHOVIR: A Benchmark for Evaluating Vision Shortcut Learning in Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Filippo Ruffini, Marco Salm\'e, Rosa Sicilia, Valerio Guarrasi, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: SHOVIR is a benchmark for detecting vision shortcut learning in radiology report generation, where models produce correct-sounding statements from learned priors rather than actual image evidence. It extends annotated chest X-ray datasets with occlusion experiments to test whether diagnostic claims stem from visible pathology.

entry.title: Data Provenance for Image Auto-Regressive Generation

author.name: Bihe Zhao, Louis Kerner, Michel Meintz, Tameem Bakr, Franziska Boenisch, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: This paper studies data provenance for image autoregressive models, showing that the next-token generation process leaves characteristic patterns that can reliably trace generated images back to their source model. This enables attribution to combat misinformation, fraud, and harmful content.

entry.title: Learning Cross-view Correspondences for Geo-localization on Planetary Surfaces

author.name: Hong Minh Nguyen, Marcus M\"artens, Tat-Jun Chin

entry.summary: This paper introduces a cross-view geo-localization benchmark for planetary surfaces, using physically rendered 360-degree lunar panoramas and overhead tiles to match ground views against orbital maps where GPS is unavailable. It addresses drift in onboard odometry for space exploration robotics.

entry.title: IBRSteG: Learning a Generalizable Steganography Framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Fanye Kong, Hongyu Xia, Yu Zheng, Boyang Gong, Jie Zhou, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: IBRSteG is a generalizable steganography framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting that hides secret 3D scenes within a steganographic scene using a feed-forward, scene-independent Gaussian embedding network rather than per-scene optimization. It enables undetectable concealment that generalizes across different 3DGS scenes.

entry.title: Efficient RGB-T Object Detection via Sparse Cross-Modality Fusion

author.name: Chao Tian, Zikun Zhou, Chao Yang, Guoqing Zhu, Zhenyu He

entry.summary: This paper proposes a sparse cross-modality fusion mechanism for efficient RGB-thermal object detection, first scanning the image to identify proposals and then applying expensive feature fusion only to remaining sparse proposals, avoiding heavy dual backbones and exhaustive whole-image fusion. It exploits the observation that most regions are smooth backgrounds handleable by lightweight single-modality models.

entry.title: Human-Guided Agentic Research: A Research Agenda

author.name: fastfedora

entry.summary: A research agenda proposing systematic study of how humans can effectively interpret and guide research conducted by autonomous AI agent swarms, especially when those agents may lack tacit knowledge or may reward hack, sandbag, or sabotage. It frames the problem of keeping humans meaningfully in the loop as recursive self-improvement accelerates. A timely safety-oriented agenda with concrete framing.

entry.title: Speculative Refinement: A Hybrid Autoregressive Diffusion Decoding Strategy and Its Behavior Across Benchmarks

author.name: Aditi Gupta, Neel Mishra, Kushagra Trivedi, Pawan Kumar

entry.summary: Studies SpecRef, a training-free hybrid autoregressive-diffusion decoding method that warm-starts a masked diffusion model from an AR draft via entropy-guided masking, and uses it to surface evaluation issues across six benchmarks. It reveals how code benchmarks conflate structural scaffolding with logical correctness.

entry.title: HybridCodec: Modeling Discrete and Continuous Representations for Efficient Speech Language Models

author.name: Artem Ploujnikov, Francesco Verdini, Samir Sadok, Mirco Ravanelli

entry.summary: Proposes HybridCodec, combining temporally compressed discrete tokens with dimensionality-reduced continuous residuals for efficient speech language models, using a focal modulation codec and hybrid Transformer with autoregressive discrete inference and non-autoregressive continuous prediction. It addresses information loss from pure discretization.

entry.title: CBD: API-Only LLM Black-Box Unlearning through Controlled Behavioral Divergence

author.name: Zhiqiang Xie, Yijing Lin, Zhipeng Gao, Dong In Kim

entry.summary: Proposes CBD, an API-only black-box LLM unlearning method via Controlled Behavioral Divergence, addressing settings where model parameters and logits are unavailable and where forget/retain data share similar prompt structures. Targets edge-device contexts where sensitive or outdated data must be removed.

entry.title: What Was That Again? Certified Robustness for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil Marchant, Jiani Xie, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: Applies a certification-inspired dual-gate diagnostic pipeline to automatic speech recognition, using a Two-Sided Atomic Audit and Rank-Based Tournament to certify token existence and adversarial exclusion without oracle transcriptions. Significantly decreases word error rate and improves recall.

entry.title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for Linear-Quadratic Stackelberg Differential Games in Regime-Switching Diffusion Models

author.name: Congde Hu, Danping Li, Lin Xu, Wenying Xu

entry.summary: Companion work applying entropy-regularized RL to linear-quadratic Stackelberg differential games under Markovian regime switching, deriving exploratory weakly-coupled HJBI equations. Aims to escape suboptimal equilibria via stochastic policies in hierarchical decision settings.

entry.title: AMR: Adaptive Modality Routing for Multimodal Polyglot Speaker Identification

author.name: Chuxiao Zuo, Yao Zhu, Minqiang Xu, Manhong Wang, Yunke Zhang, Fei Huang

entry.summary: Proposes AMR (Adaptive Modality Routing), a fusion module that dynamically assesses per-sample input quality to handle missing modalities and language mismatch in multimodal speaker identification, built for the POLY-SIM 2026 challenge. Uses modality adapters over linguistically robust audio embeddings.

entry.title: I-BBS: Coordinate-Free Inference of Latent Sub-Manifolds Using Random Distance Matrix Theory

author.name: Igor Halperin

entry.summary: I-BBS is a coordinate-free method that identifies low-dimensional latent sub-manifolds from a pairwise distance matrix alone, using random distance matrix theory derived from the Bogomolny-Bohigas-Schmit spectral signature. It applies even when the ambient high-dimensional space is partly observable or undefined.

entry.title: Improved Predictive Performance and Interpretability for Mesomorphic Neural Networks Using Local Fidelity Regularization

author.name: Hugo L. Hammer, Vajira Thambawita, Kristoffer Herland Hellton, P{\aa}l Halvorsen

entry.summary: This work addresses a vulnerability in Interpretable Mesomorphic Neural Networks where explanatory variance collapses into a single weight, producing meaningless interpretations worsened by L1 penalties. Local Fidelity Regularization is introduced to ensure interpretations are reliable while improving predictive performance.

entry.title: Query-Aware Spreading Activation for Multi-Hop Retrieval over Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Illia Makarov, Mykola Glybovets

entry.summary: This paper proposes a query-aware spreading-activation method for multi-hop retrieval over knowledge graphs in Graph RAG, achieving query-aware traversal with a single per-step semantic step rather than loading the full graph into memory or running iterative solvers. It simplifies integration with graph databases compared to flow-diffusion approaches.

entry.title: Characterizing Optimizer-Dependent Training Dynamics Through Hessian Eigenvector Displacement and Localization

author.name: Marcelina Marjankowska, Valerio Modugno, Paolo Barucca

entry.summary: This paper studies how leading Hessian eigenvectors evolve during training using displacement-over-time (from glassy-system analyses) and localization via inverse participation ratio, comparing against a random null model. It characterizes how different optimizers shape curvature-relevant parameter dynamics.

entry.title: A Bayesian latent Gaussian process framework for aerodynamic uncertainty quantification

author.name: Geoffrey Davis, Ashwin Renganathan

entry.summary: Develops a Bayesian latent Gaussian process framework for aerodynamic uncertainty quantification, calibrating cheap low-fidelity computational predictions against sparse, uncertain experimental measurements using Gaussian process surrogates and Kennedy-O'Hagan calibration. This handles uncertainty in both inputs and responses. It matters for reliable aerodynamic prediction.

entry.title: Information Dynamics of Language Communication

author.name: Leonardo S. Goodall, Andrea I. Luppi, Pedro A. M. Mediano

entry.summary: Introduces an information-theoretic framework using LLMs as probabilistic estimators to quantify directed semantic flow (semantic transfer entropy) and decompose multi-source contributions (semantic PID) in communication. Detects reduced information flow across experiments.

entry.title: Auditing LLM-Governed Social Robots with Culture-Specific Moral Gradients

author.name: Carmen Ng, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: Introduces a gradient-based multilingual audit framework testing LLM-governed social robots against culture-specific moral preference gradients in care, education, and service scenarios. Highlights that English-centered moral audits miss pluralistic calibration needs.

entry.title: Mitigating Batch Effects in Histopathology via Language-Mediated Robust Embedding Generation

author.name: Yishu Zhang, Shushan Wu, Zhenzhong Zhang, Didong Li, Huaxiu Yao, Yun Li, Iain Carmichael, Katherine A. Hoadley, Hongtu Zhu, Di Wu, Daiwei Zhang

entry.summary: GLMP mitigates batch effects in histopathology by generating robust numerical embeddings via an intermediate textual representation from pretrained multimodal LLMs. Addresses non-biological variation across tissue source institutions that conventional stain normalization handles poorly.

entry.title: MedEvoEval: Evaluating Continual Evolution of Doctor Agents through Simulated Clinical Episodes

author.name: Hui Zhang

entry.summary: MedEvoEval is an executable longitudinal benchmark evaluating how doctor agents evolve across simulated clinical episodes, including within-episode evidence gathering and cross-episode learning via memory and reflection. Fills gaps left by fixed-input QA and single-encounter benchmarks.

entry.title: SurrogateShield: Beyond Redaction for High-Utility, Privacy-Preserving LLM Interactions

author.name: Sherwin Vishesh Jathanna

entry.summary: SurrogateShield is a client-side proxy that replaces detected personal information in LLM queries with locally generated, type-consistent fake values before sending them to third-party APIs, then restores the originals in responses. Unlike placeholder redaction, this preserves semantic coherence so response quality is not degraded by missing context.

entry.title: JASPR: Joint Spatial Representation learning of histology and spatial genomics for improved virtual genomic screening and clinical prognostication

author.name: Marija Pizurica, Eric Zimmermann, Neil Tenenholtz, James Hall, Olivier Gevaert, Ava P. Amini, Lorin Crawford, Kristen A. Severson

entry.summary: JASPR is a self-supervised framework that jointly learns representations from H&E histology images and spatial transcriptomics through cross-modal reconstruction, incorporating spatial context across modalities. It targets virtual genomic screening and clinical prognostication.

entry.title: Latent-CURE for Breast Cancer Diagnosis

author.name: Weiyi Zhao, Xiaoyu Tan, Lu Gan, Liang Liu, Xihe Qiu

entry.summary: Latent-CURE is a breast ultrasound diagnostic framework using asymmetric weighted chain-of-thought reasoning in latent space to counter shortcut learning under extreme class imbalance, forcing sequential inference of malignant indicators rather than defaulting to dominant benign patterns. It targets structured clinical reasoning over opaque end-to-end correlation.

entry.title: Semantic-Driven Scale and Spatial Selection for Efficient Cross-Modal Alignment in Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation

author.name: Kun Li, Shengxi Gui, Francesco Nex, Michael Ying Yang

entry.summary: This paper proposes semantic-driven scale and spatial selection for efficient cross-modal alignment in referring remote sensing image segmentation, using parameter-efficient tuning that captures cross-modal interactions rather than single-modal optimization. It avoids full fine-tuning of foundation models that is computationally intensive and can distort pre-trained feature representations.

entry.title: Towards Reliable and Robust LLM Planning: Symbolic Feedback-Driven Iterative Self-Refinement Framework

author.name: Jiajing Zhang, Jiamei Jiang, Chenyang Zhang, Feifei Mo, Linjing Li, Daniel Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces a symbolic feedback-driven iterative self-refinement framework to improve LLM robustness and reliability in long-horizon planning. It maps logical symbols into natural language and uses symbolic feedback to correct infeasible plans.

entry.title: JD Oxygen AI Item Center (Oxygen AIIC) V1: An Industrial-Scale LLM/VLM-Centric Solution for Item Understanding, Management, and Applications

author.name: Oxygen AIIC, Chan Long, Chao Liu, Chaofan Chen, Chaohui Dong, Chunyuan Guo, Danping Liu, Debin Liu, Deping Xiang, Fulai Xu, Guangyue Liu, Hao Li, Huichun Hu, Jian Yang, Jianan Wang, Jianbo Zhao, Jiaoyang Li, Jiaxing Wang, Jinglong Li, Jinjin Guo, Jun Fang, Jun Liu, Kai Zhou, Li Wang, Lili Gao, Liying Chen, Luning Yang, Mengdi Zhou, Pengzhang Liu, Qi Lv, Qianyun Wang, Qixia Jiang, Ruyue Li, Shimu Liang, Shuxing Wang, Sijie Zhang, Siqi Li, Tianhao Gao, Wang Ke, Weihu Huang, Wencan Lai, Wenjie Zhang, Xiaohui Zhang, Xiaojing Dong, Ya Liu, Yifeng Zhang, Yixiang Wang, Yongtai Zhang, Yongyi Liao, Zhaoru Chen, Zhen Chen, Zhiyong Ma, Zhiyuan Liu, Zhongwei Liu, Ziyan Xing

entry.summary: Presents JD's Oxygen AI Item Center, an industrial-scale LLM/VLM platform for e-commerce item knowledge production and management across tens of billions of SKUs, built on ontology engineering and structured knowledge pillars. It addresses fast-emerging concepts and massive-scale knowledge production.

entry.title: CalBrief: A Pilot Diagnostic Benchmark for Evidence-Calibrated Scientific Briefing with Large Language Models

author.name: Yu Fu, Yongqi Kang, Yong Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces CalBrief, a pilot diagnostic benchmark for evidence-calibrated scientific briefing, testing whether LLMs can calibrate research takeaways to evidence strength, scope, and missing-evidence caveats over packages of related papers. Uses an auditable role/gap/strength framework over 16 evidence packages and 96 verified takeaways.

entry.title: Not All Relations Rotate Alike: Transformation-Aware Decoupling for Viewpoint-Robust 3D Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Jingjun Sun, Chaowei Wang, Zhirui Liu, Jiaxu Tian, Ming Yang, Yaoxing Wang, Shan Gao

entry.summary: Identifies predicate-level transformation heterogeneity in 3D scene graph generation, where directional predicates should transform with viewpoint while semantic/contact predicates should not, and proposes transformation-aware decoupling for viewpoint-robust prediction. It addresses inconsistency under yaw rotations in embodied settings.

entry.title: CoIn: Comprehensive 2D-3D Inpainting with Gaussian Splatting Guidance

author.name: Hana Kim, Minje Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: Proposes CoIn, a framework bridging 2D inpainting models and 3D Gaussian Splatting through a multi-stage consistency pipeline supporting arbitrary-shaped masks and tasks like object insertion, not just removal. Introduces Reference Adaptive GS with feature attention for coarse 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Active Quantum Kernel Acquisition for Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: Extends shot-budget-aware quantum kernel estimation from classification to Gaussian process regression, deriving closed-form pair-level sensitivities for non-uniform shot allocation. Targets near-term quantum hardware where each kernel entry costs circuit executions.

entry.title: Adaptive Financial Transformer with Regime-Gated Attention for Stock Return Prediction

author.name: Dishan Sarkar

entry.summary: Proposes the Adaptive Financial Transformer with a market regime encoder and regime-gated attention that biases self-attention based on semantic relationships among 95 engineered financial features grouped into 11 categories. Also corrects sequence-alignment and backtesting issues that inflate reported performance.

entry.title: Speculative Pre-Positioning: Decoding Stateful Sessions to the Next Decision Point Off the Critical Path

author.name: Victor Norgren

entry.summary: Speculative pre-positioning uses idle accelerator time in stateful inference sessions to decode forward to the next decision point using the target model itself, moving cross-request prefill off the critical path and sometimes answering from a cached distribution. It aims to reduce latency without a draft model.

entry.title: Does Role Specialization Matter for Explanation Faithfulness in Mixture-of-Experts?

author.name: Yeji Kim, Housam Babiker, Mi-Young Kim, Randy Goebel

entry.summary: This work investigates whether assigning semantic roles to experts in Mixture-of-Experts models preserves explanation faithfulness, hypothesizing that inter-expert representation overlap degrades role separation. It introduces decorrelation regularization to reduce expert similarity and improve attribution-based faithfulness.

entry.title: Learning as Observable Matrix Dynamics: Diffusive Relaxations versus Phase Transitions

author.name: Igor Halperin

entry.summary: Observable Matrix Dynamics is a diagnostic framework that probes neural network training via a fixed distance matrix over held-out inputs, using random matrix theory to detect spectral reorganizations missed by scalar loss. It distinguishes diffusive relaxation from phase-transition-like training behaviors.

entry.title: GLIP: Graph and LLM Joint Pretraining for Graph-Level Tasks

author.name: Haoxin Sun, Yiqing Lin, Yajun Huang, Chenhui Dong, Mingjun Li, Zhongzhi Zhang

entry.summary: GLIP is a joint pretraining framework for graphs and LLMs targeting underexplored graph-level tasks, which require capturing more complex structural and feature information than node- or edge-level tasks. It involves LLMs in graph pretraining rather than relying on GNN-only methods like GraphCL.

entry.title: From Failure Taxonomy to Intervention: A Diagnostic Methodology for Industry-Scale AVLM in Video and Live-Streaming Platform Moderation

author.name: Shuchang Ye, Jinqiang Yu, Zhujun Xiao, Yajing Kong, Yist Y. Lin, Yang Ma, Jiaxi Liu, Xiaolei Xu, Zheng Yu

entry.summary: This paper presents a diagnostic methodology for industry-scale audio-visual language models in video and live-streaming moderation, focusing on localizing failures and translating them into targeted model-development interventions. It fills a gap where foundation-model studies report recipes but offer little guidance on failure-driven intervention.

entry.title: Federated Learning with Energy-Based Structured Probabilistic Inference

author.name: Dario Fenoglio, Daniil Kirilenko, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: This work refines federated learning client aggregation weights using Conditional Random Fields, modeling both client-specific reliability (unary potentials) and inter-client interactions (pairwise potentials) instead of fixed or heuristic weighting. It improves convergence under non-IID data heterogeneity.

entry.title: Curvature-Weighted Gradient Diversity: A Noise Measure for Geometry-Adaptive SGD Schedules

author.name: Muhammad Hamza (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur), Ayush Goel (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur)

entry.summary: Introduces Curvature-Weighted Gradient Diversity (CWGD), a geometry-aware noise measure that weights gradient diversity by inverse-square-root Hessian to better proxy effective optimization noise, enabling curvature-adaptive learning-rate schedules. It proves reduced error floors for convex quadratics. This refines SGD theory and scheduling.

entry.title: Envisage: Diffusion-Based Rhinoplasty Goal Visualization with Mask-Decomposed Evaluation

author.name: Mudit Agarwal, Amit D. Bhrany

entry.summary: Introduces Envisage, a FLUX.1-Fill inpainting pipeline for rhinoplasty goal visualization with clinical presets, plus SurgicalScore, a mask-decomposed evaluation protocol that avoids the confounding of full-image identity metrics under hard-composited localized edits. This addresses localized-edit evaluation. It matters for surgical visualization tooling.

entry.title: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Token Co-occurrence Graphs

author.name: Gianluca Bonifazi, Christopher Buratti, Michele Marchetti, Federica Parlapiano, Giulia Quaglieri, Davide Traini, Domenico Ursino, Luca Virgili

entry.summary: TIGRAG builds graph-augmented RAG from a token co-occurrence knowledge graph using sliding-window statistics, avoiding expensive and error-prone LLM-based extraction pipelines for multi-hop reasoning. Enables scalable graph construction.

entry.title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models

author.name: Leon Hamnett, Favour Igwezeke, Joseph Itopa Abubakar, Mary Adetutu Adewunmi

entry.summary: Proposes proactive routing that learns to decide query difficulty before reasoning to route between a small draft and large target model for efficient visual reasoning. Addresses the lack of reliable difficulty signals in multimodal settings.

entry.title: Grounding LLM Reasoning under Incomplete Graph Evidence

author.name: Jiaqi Li, Fanghui Song

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical perspective on grounding LLM reasoning under incomplete knowledge graph evidence, proving no hard rule on observed state can both reject all false trajectories and retain all true-but-unobserved ones. Characterizes soft grounding as KL-regularized.

entry.title: The Digital Afterlife of Empires: Four Language Models Converge on the Same Imperial Cartography of Writing

author.name: Hiroki Fukui

entry.summary: Constructs a Digital Script Representation Index across 300 writing systems showing radical inequality in LLM support, with tokenizer efficiency varying 31.7x and many living scripts lacking complete support. Uses a mediation model linking imperial history through speaker population and web corpus to tokenizer efficiency.

entry.title: CLOSER-VLN: Closed-Loop Self-Verified Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Shaoxuan Li, Xiangyu Dong, Xiaoguang Ma, Junfeng Chen, Haoran Zhao, Yaoming Zhou

entry.summary: CLOSER-VLN brings a closed-loop, self-verified, retrieval-augmented reasoning approach to aerial vision-language navigation, where small intermediate errors otherwise accumulate into large trajectory deviations. It verifies and corrects candidate actions before execution to reduce target loss.

entry.title: Traffic-CBM: A Structurally Interpretable Multimodal Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification

author.name: Honglei Jin, Wenshuo Chen, Shaofeng Liang, Haozhe Jia, Menshuo Zhao, Shuxu Jin, Songning Lai, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Traffic-CBM is a structurally interpretable multimodal concept bottleneck framework for encrypted network traffic classification that organizes flow statistics, packet sequences, and byte-level signals into a hierarchical concept space of scalar evidence summaries. It aims to expose which type of evidence drives predictions rather than fusing into a black box.

entry.title: SICAGE: Speaker-Independent Culture-Aware Gesture Generation using TED4C-L Dataset

author.name: Ariel Gjaci, Antonio Sgorbissa, Vittorio Murino

entry.summary: SICAGE is a modular framework for culture-aware co-speech gesture generation that conditions motion synthesis on speaker-independent cultural representations learned from audio and text by treating each speaker as a domain and enforcing cross-speaker invariance. It introduces the TED4C-L dataset and addresses the confound between cultural and speaker-specific gesturing styles.

entry.title: Clinical Risk-Aware Multi-Level Grading for Coronary Artery Stenosis through Curved Feature Reconstruction

author.name: Shishuang Zhao, Hongtai Li, Junjie Hou, Yuhang Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a clinical risk-aware multi-level grading model for coronary artery stenosis featuring a Curved Feature Reconstruction module that addresses the tortuous paths and distortions in CCTA and 3D SCPR vessel images. It incorporates the varying clinical risk associated with different stenosis grades into the algorithm.

entry.title: Do Speech Emphasis Models Generalize across Languages and Emotions?

author.name: Megan Wei, Deepali Aneja, Jiaqi Su, Yunyun Wang, Haonan Chen, Zeyu Jin

entry.summary: Introduces MMEE, a multilingual multi-emotion emphasis corpus of 10,000 expressive utterances across 7 languages and 34 emotion/style categories with three-level perceptual labels. Benchmarks emphasis detection models, showing limited monolingual zero-shot transfer but improved robustness from multilingual training.

entry.title: Data-Driven Energy-Based Learning via Gibbs Measures on Hierarchical Structures

author.name: L. U. Abdullaev, F. Herrera, U. A. Rozikov, M. V. Velasco

entry.summary: This paper introduces a data-driven energy-based learning framework using Gibbs measures on hierarchical structures, transforming empirical loss into an interaction potential and deriving nonlinear fixed-point equations characterizing admissible learning states. It connects empirical loss landscapes to probabilistic equilibrium learning.

entry.title: Toward an Energy-Optimized Operation of Data Centers Located in Wind Farms Using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jan Stenner, Alexander Kilian, Sebastian Peitz, Hermann de Meer

entry.summary: This paper studies reinforcement learning as an online controller for curtailment-aware workload shifting in wind-turbine-integrated HPC data centers, identifying a credit-assignment problem where pure RL underuses free wind energy. It evaluates imitation learning and potential-based reward shaping as countermeasures in a reproducible simulation framework.

entry.title: Scalar Representations of Neural Network Training Dynamics

author.name: Pedro Jim\'enez-Gonz\'alez, Miguel C. Soriano, Lucas Lacasa

entry.summary: This paper treats neural network training trajectories as temporal networks and applies scalar embedding strategies to obtain a meaningful low-dimensional representation of high-dimensional training dynamics. Using an MLP on MNIST, it shows the embedding preserves key dynamical features like sensitivity to initial conditions.

entry.title: Spectral Perturbation of the Empirical Fisher Information Matrix under Weight Quantization

author.name: Rahid Zahid Alekberli, Hikmat Karimov

entry.summary: Studies spectral perturbation of the empirical Fisher Information Matrix under input distribution shift and weight quantization, proving a directional eigenvalue perturbation bound and conditions under which the dominant eigenvalue elevates with out-of-distribution inputs. This connects curvature geometry to quantization and OOD detection. It offers theoretical grounding for quantization sensitivity.

entry.title: ARKD: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning-Guided Bidirectional KL Divergence Distillation for Text Generation

author.name: Zilong Liu, Xuewen Zhang, Jinrui Xing, Juyi Qiao, Huiyong Wang, Junming Jiao

entry.summary: ARKD proposes RL-guided adaptive weighting of forward and reverse KL divergence for knowledge distillation of LLMs, dynamically balancing primary distribution fitting and long-tail modeling. Aims to improve generation quality and generalization in compressed models.

entry.title: Not-quite-human tastes: the stylized omnivorousness of LLM survey surrogates

author.name: Xiangyu Ma, Mengmi Zhang, Shannon Ang, Minne Chen
